Phase 1 was a dry run of the whole pipeline on three Lock⁵ case studies. Each
note follows the same skeleton: question → published study → dataset → several
statistical methods (parametric + randomization + bootstrap) → decision.

| Question | Note | Headline result |
|---|---|---|
| Is there a "sprinting gene"? | [Sprinting Gene](sprinting_gene.qmd) | ACTN3 R577X: χ² = 19.54, p < 0.0001; XX genotype rare in sprinters (5.6% vs 18.3%) |
| Does tagging penguins harm them? | [Penguin Tagging](penguin_tagging.qmd) | 20% vs 36% survival; z p = 0.037 but randomization p = 0.057 → suggestive, not decisive |
| Do humans emit pheromones? | [Pheromones](pheromones.qmd) | Estratetraenol shifts gender perception; t(71) = 2.49, p = 0.0075, CI excludes 0 |

## What Phase 1 established

- A repeatable note template: **Question → Data source → EDA → Methods →
  Decision**, always pairing parametric tests with non-parametric validation
  (randomization / bootstrap, 100k replicates, seed 2026).
- Data provenance discipline: every note states whether the CSV is published
  counts, digitized means, or a documented reconstruction.
- Automatic publishing to GitHub Pages on every push to `master`
  ([site](https://math4mad.github.io/Lock5Stat-by-AI/)).

Phase 2 scaled the same workflow to 17 questions in parallel — see the
[Phase 2 index](../phase2/index.qmd).
